data.narrative:
Merge Labs is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Sam Altman and five others, having raised $252M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in Biotech & Health, though direct peer multiples cannot be reliably applied due to data constraints.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. This approach uses the $252M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for progression from seed to next-stage financing, yielding an implied valuation of $630M. Peer-median analysis was not feasible: while 7 same-sector peers exist, none satisfied the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or comparable-tier comparison, leaving an insufficient subset for robust medians. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (7.4x median across the three tickers) could not be deployed because the target's revenue is not disclosed, which is standard for private companies at this stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $536M to $724M, with $630M as the midpoint estimate. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier for this founder team and sector, the absence of revenue data for alternative approaches, and the thinness of directly comparable seed-stage biotech benchmarks.
